title: A requirement for documentation
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
It has come to my attention that a written record of my research is required.

I am fulfilling this demand...

Research concerning Subject C-25 has not progressed as much as I would have preferred.

The subject's insistence upon serving as a behavioral chaperone is becoming bothersome.

I would prefer to conduct my work without Subject C-25 constantly evaluating me.

The subject is...

relentlessly observant.

I am growing increasingly convinced that Subject C-25 has developed some manner of psychic ability.

Whether I am awake or sleeping...

Subject C-25 seems to be aware.

More troublingly, it appears to have formed opinions regarding my behavior.

I have found no satisfactory explanation for this.

Suggested action: Shelve Subject C-25 until a later date.

A long nap may relax the subject...

and would permit me to work without supervision.

For now...

Subject H-31 shows considerably more promise.

H-31 appears decidedly more agreeable, provided sweets are offered in recompense.

The response has been remarkably consistent.

No sweets...

little cooperation.

Sweets...

considerably more cooperation.

Further study is required, of course.

However...

I find myself cautiously optimistic.

Subject H-31 may prove to be the success story this Institute needs.

title: Today belongs to the rat
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
No changes in Subject H-31 and yet...

... documentation is still required.

I lost a cufflink today.

The lunch provided by the institute provided little inspiration.

It is currently raining.

The laboratory cat, Baryon, offered a rat to me.

The rat then ran away.

Today is not a day for science.

Today belongs to the rat.

title: Concerning confectionery
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
Progress has been made with Subject H-31.

It seems H-31 has...

... preferences.

When offered a sweet from Reese Laboratory, Subject H-31 responds with enthusiasm.

Though...

... when offered a peanut taffy, Subject H-31 recoils.

To be thorough I tested H-31 with both the orange ones and then with the black ones.

This fits my larger hypothesis that no creature enjoys the orange and black taffy.

The confection industry shall be shaken with this finding.

Though I feel future generations will be thankful for these findings.

Subject H-31 seems to have generated an affinity for the laboratory windows as of late.

All goes well, Subject H-31 and I shall explore the institute grounds.

My next move is to inform Dr. Melster that his orange and black confections are an abomination.

Perhaps I shall word it differently...

... perhaps I won't

title: Instructions for Jeff
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
Subject H-31 grows more animated.

It is hard to gauge if this behavior is curiosity or agitation.

Thankfully a Reese Confection continues to remedy this behavior.

I have asked the institute custodian, Jeff, to remove the orange and black taffy from the premises.

I find it doubtful that Jeff will follow my instructions fully, though.

I informed Jeff to remove them, take them outside...

burn them...

then put out the fire with the posterior end of Dr. Melster.

I will settle for the taffy being removed.

Subject H-31 has continued observing the birds as they fly by.

If Subject H-31 continues this behavior and a hunting cap becomes involved...

... termination of experiment will happen post-haste.

Observations shall continue.

title: Mistakes were made
date: The Morning Immediately Following a Thursday
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
It appears that, in my haste yesterday, I absent-mindedly neglected to lock Subject H-31's enclosure.

Mistakes were made.

Questions have been answered.

I can now conclude that the structural integrity of the subject appears to be superior...

... to that of the laboratory window.

It is safe to conclude that Subject H-31 was not interested in birds...

... Subject H-31 was learning how to fly.

I am also moved to the conclusion that Subject H-31 was more curious than agitated.

This finding is favorable.

I must also conclude that Subject H-31 has flown off with what was going to be my breakfast.

This finding is unfavorable.

Future journals shall be from outside of the institute.

title: A breakfast, unaccounted for
heading: The Offsite Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
I have tracked bewildered looks to a tavern near the institute.

The mood of the surrounding people is surprisingly dismissive.

The tavern window does not appear to be disturbed though the patrons seem a bit more...

... disturbed.

Upon speaking to the tavern maid Subject H-31 (whom I shall refer to as 'Gary' to ease the minds of everyone) came in...

... relieved the tavern of a breakfast.

This breakfast consisted of:

- Eggs
- Streaky bacon
- Hotcakes
- American maple syrup

Then Subject H-31 promptly left with the tavern's inventory of Reese confections.

Fortunately Subject H-31 didn't think about the wrappers and left a trail to itself.

Subject H-31 shall be remanded into my custody soon.

Upon investigation I may have been premature in assessment.

Subject H-31 is not present but it did leave something behind.

I have sent word to the institute for Jeff to come collect the specimen.

The hunt continues.

title: Who infests who?
date: The Same Month, Following an Unscheduled Rat
heading: The Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
I have arrived back at the institute.
I find myself with less to document at this point.
Baryon has brought me another rat.
The institute appears to have a rat problem.
Perhaps the rats have an institute problem.

Who infests who?
This is a discussion for a later date.
Until then I wait for the rat to spring up once Baryon has left.

...

The rat has now exited the laboratory.

I can still feel Subject C-25 passing judgement on me.

I have just received a wire from the United States.

I have been informed that Subject H-31 has been spotted...

... in the state of Maine.

I shall catch a ship at next launch.
I shall also use my newly found knowledge of Subject H-31's behavioral model...

... by taking a pocket full of Reese with me.
To Maine.
signature:
Signed
Elias Grimsby
The Grimsby Institute

title: The question of Bah-stn
heading: The Offsite Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
I have arrived in the Americas.

I believe I am in a town known as "Boston."

To ensure that my journey has not gone awry, I shall confirm with one of the locals.

My journey, as it seems, did not directly bring me to Boston.

I am in a small annex of Boston known as "Bah-stn."

For confirmation, I asked a young dockhand to spell it.

I believe the dockhand is hard of hearing.

I asked the same question, only louder and slower.

The dockhand continued to look confused.

I asked him how I get from Bah-stn to Boston.

The dockhand remained confused.

I became confused.

He remained confused.

I asked where I could procure transportation.

He pointed toward a window.

I compensated the dockhand for his time and approached the window.

I found that I could either take a coach or steamship.

I was warned that the coach would be a rather bumpy ride.

I chose the steamship.

Comfort is important.

More importantly, it is boarding now.

I shall report my findings from the ship.
signature:
Signed,

Elias Grimsby

The Grimsby Institute

title: On the nature of the ha-bah
heading: The Offsite Journal of Elias Grimsby
text:
My goodness, this ship is pungent.

Could be the air.

Could be the other passengers.

Could be some amalgamation of all variables.

I kept my Reese's close by.

I overheard passengers discussing leaving the "Ha-bah"

A Ha-Bah?

A funny sheep perhaps?

Does America have humorous livestock?

I regret not visiting this enchanted land sooner.

I simply must return when I have more time.

I am desperate to hear a sheep tell jokes.

Onward to Maine!
signature:
Signed,

Elias Grimsby

The Grimsby Institute
